visualReview.notes: All 11 current portable frames inspected, including turntable, curved inland face, pointed seaward granite spine, recessed slit windows, both roof terraces, entrance doors and anchor relief. The entrance chamfers are now closed, the seaward camera contains the entire tower, and granite block tint variation no longer creates diagonal bands. Roof guards, splayed entrance wings and the curved silhouette remain intact.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All 11 current shared-surface frames inspected. Metric clinker courses follow the curved and planar walls; independent granite blocks use the raw basalt surface without an extra masonry pattern. Darker vertex tints match the owner's clinker/granite photographs across sunlit and shaded faces. The north-up placement follows the mapped tower and splayed wings. Geographic loading and unload checks passed.

geographicReview.notes: The exact Q538382 OSM tower outline and its small entrance wings establish the native ground plan and anchor. Owner shoreline and courtyard photographs resolve the pointed granite spine northwest toward Kiel Fjord and the curved entrance southeast toward the courtyard. The reviewed north-up placement aligns that directed shape with the mapped outline. Native height uses the owner's 72 m above the foot, rather than its separate 85 m above sea-level statement. The surrounding memorial courtyard, halls and submarine are separate structures.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the complete detailed exterior in the project's polygonal reconstruction style. The published 1929 contractor section and current owner's photographs establish the curved body, rising granite spine, recessed grouped slit windows, lower and upper observation terraces, guards, dual entrance doors, anchor relief and splayed walls. Footprint and 72 m height are evidence based; intermediate heights, opening widths and individual granite block layout are proportional original reconstructions, not surveyed masonry. Current temporary scaffolding and interior spaces are outside the permanent exterior. Concrete camera, corner closure, color and repetitive stone-pattern defects were corrected and recaptured.
